vocabulary.meaning: happening at exactly the same time or in a coordinated way
examples: The swimmers performed a perfectly synchronised movement.
Synchronised routines require many hours of practice.

vocabulary.meaning: a planned sequence of movements in a performance
examples: The team created a new routine for the competition.
The routine lasted several minutes.

vocabulary.meaning: the design and arrangement of movements in dance or performance
examples: The choreography combined swimming and dance.
Complex choreography is difficult to perform in water.

vocabulary.meaning: the physical ability to continue an activity for a long time
examples: Artistic swimming requires great stamina.
Regular training improves stamina.

vocabulary.meaning: the ability of the body to bend and move easily
examples: The sport demands strength and flexibility.
Stretching can improve flexibility.

vocabulary.meaning: the ability to manage breathing during physical activity
examples: Swimmers need excellent breath control.
Breath-control exercises are part of training.

vocabulary.meaning: the ability to work effectively with others
examples: Successful routines depend on teamwork.
The athletes develop strong teamwork during practice.
Judges reward precision in every movement.
The swimmers moved with impressive precision.

vocabulary.meaning: an official who scores or evaluates a performance
examples: The judges awarded high scores for technique.
Each judge watches different aspects of the routine.

vocabulary.meaning: physically strong, fit, and skilled in sport
examples: Artistic swimmers are highly athletic.
The performance combines artistic and athletic skills.
